title: Eccentric-orbit extreme-mass-ratio inspiral gravitational wave energy fluxes to 7PN order
central_claims: High-precision black-hole perturbation calculations yield new analytic and numerical eccentric-orbit energy-flux terms from 3.5PN through 7PN.
High-order hereditary expansions and eccentricity singular factors improve flux representation toward large eccentricity.

source_manifest.title: Eccentric-orbit extreme-mass-ratio inspiral gravitational wave energy fluxes to 7PN order
source_manifest.finding: New mixed analytic/numerical terms through 7PN and singular-factor treatment of hereditary functions; fitting is limited in PN and eccentricity order.

source_manifest.title: Hereditary Effects in Eccentric Compact Binary Inspirals to Third Post-Newtonian Order
source_manifest.finding: Section 4 follows the original singular-factor procedure, then adds high-order series and Pade approximants for energy and angular-momentum hereditary terms. The introduction cautions that truncated small-eccentricity resummations need enough terms.

source_manifest.title: Determination of new coefficients in the angular momentum and energy fluxes at infinity to 9PN order for eccentric Schwarzschild extreme-mass-ratio inspirals using mode-by-mode fitting
source_manifest.finding: The original authors and Munna extend the fitting approach to mode-level calculations, angular momentum and higher PN order. Computational complexity limits further nonlogarithmic terms.

source_manifest.title: Post-Newtonian theory for gravitational waves
source_manifest.finding: Sections on eccentric fluxes retain the high-PN results and explicitly explain the singular-factor method, its convergence and usefulness near unit eccentricity.

source_manifest.title: Second-Post-Newtonian Energy and Angular Momentum Fluxes for Eccentric Inspirals in Effective-One-Body Formalism via Coordinate Transformation
source_manifest.finding: Zhang and Han check their test-particle coordinate conversion against original equations 5.1–5.2. This checks low-order reference relations, not the novel 7PN flux coefficients.

answers.rationale: Independent work applies the singular-factor method, but a matched confirmation of the full novel 3.5–7PN coefficient set was not verified.
Neither the hereditary extension nor the low-order coordinate check reproduces the complete 7PN construction.
The 9PN extension shares the original team and changes the fitting procedure; no independent stricter test of the whole result was located.
Blanchet retains both the high-PN contribution and the singular-factor improvement in an authoritative review.
Later work discusses truncation and computation costs, but does not explicitly test and resolve all original applicability limits.
Loutrel and Yunes extend the singular-factor procedure to their hereditary-flux approximants.
One clear independent extension was established; the 2026 low-order reference check is not a second extension of the novel contribution.
The independent hereditary calculation explicitly follows the original factoring procedure.
The review identifies a methodological advance and applications, but not a distinct research direction enabled by this paper.
The 2026 check uses low-order relations reproduced in the paper, not a benchmark of its novel 7PN or factoring contribution.
Applying the factoring procedure enables independent analytic approximants for otherwise difficult hereditary terms.
The procedure is used for angular-momentum as well as energy hereditary terms in the later calculation.
The adopted factoring step contributes directly to new high-order hereditary approximants.
No verified detector-analysis workflow or production waveform implementation was attributable to this particular result.
Later approximants combine additional techniques; no isolated fair comparison establishes the original method’s claimed advantage.
The 2020 extension builds directly on the original fitting program four years after publication.
The 2024 review explicitly credits the central singular-factor improvement and retains the high-PN results.
Independent methodological use in 2017 and substantive synthesis in 2024 document distinct later years.
The review explains the method and its convergent series as accepted tools for eccentric fluxes.
Continued review coverage does not itself establish an explicit comparison showing usefulness despite newer alternatives.

search_gaps: No complete independent reproduction of the novel 7PN coefficient set was verified.
Low-order coordinate checks and same-author extensions were not counted as independent full-result validation.
No detector operational adoption attributable specifically to this paper was verified.
research.summary: The singular-factor method is explicitly reused in independent hereditary calculations and retained in a 2024 review. The original team extends the numerical program to 9PN. Complete independent replication of the novel coefficient set and operational deployment remain unverified.
